title: The Great Crash
overview: In 2008 the world suffers its worst financial crisis since the Great Depression. A boom in risky American home loans turns to bust, and on 15 September the Wall Street bank Lehman Brothers goes bankrupt, freezing credit around the globe. Governments spend vast sums rescuing banks, stock markets crash, and the world slides into a deep downturn soon called the Great Recession. Earlier in the year, soaring food prices set off protests and riots in dozens of poorer countries, and oil peaks at about $147 a barrel in July before collapsing to near $30 by December. The crisis hastens a shift in global power: in November the leaders of the G20, which includes China, India and Brazil, meet for the first time to steer the world economy. The United States, still at war in Iraq and Afghanistan after the attacks of 11 September 2001, elects Barack Obama as its first African American president. China hosts a spectacular Olympic Games in Beijing, Russia fights a short war with Georgia, Kosovo declares independence, a cyclone devastates Myanmar, an earthquake kills some 69,000 people in China, and in November gunmen attack Mumbai.

regions.southern-africa: South Africa's ruling ANC forces President Thabo Mbeki to resign in September, and Kgalema Motlanthe takes over until the 2009 election. Zimbabwe's economy has collapsed into hyperinflation; after a disputed election in March, opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai pulls out of a violent June run-off, leaving Robert Mugabe in power until a power-sharing deal is signed in September. In Kenya, violence after the disputed December 2007 election kills over a thousand people before Mwai Kibaki and Raila Odinga agree to share power. In the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, ruled by Joseph Kabila, Laurent Nkunda's rebels push towards the city of Goma late in the year.
regions.northern-africa: In Sudan, where the Darfur conflict has driven millions from their homes, the International Criminal Court's prosecutor asks in July for an arrest warrant against President Omar al-Bashir. Somalia's weak transitional government depends on Ethiopian troops against the Islamist al-Shabaab insurgency, while pirates off the Somali coast attack over a hundred ships during the year. Soaring food prices bring protests and riots to Egypt, ruled by Hosni Mubarak, and to Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Senegal and other countries. Military coups topple the governments of Mauritania in August and Guinea in December, the day after the death of its long-time ruler Lansana Conte. Muammar Gaddafi's Libya has restored full relations with the United States, and Umaru Yar'Adua is Nigeria's president.
regions.europe: Europe is hit hard by the crisis: Britain nationalises the bank Northern Rock in February and pours billions into its other banks in October, and in October all three of Iceland's big banks collapse, wrecking its economy. Kosovo declares independence from Serbia in February; it is recognised by many Western countries but not by Serbia or Russia. In August, Russia and Georgia fight a five-day war over South Ossetia, after which Russia recognises South Ossetia and Abkhazia as independent states. Dmitry Medvedev becomes Russia's president in May, with Vladimir Putin as his prime minister. Angela Merkel leads Germany, Nicolas Sarkozy France, Gordon Brown Britain, and Silvio Berlusconi returns to power in Italy.
regions.middle-east-south-asia: Violence in Iraq is falling after the 2007 US troop 'surge', and in November the two governments agree that US forces will leave by the end of 2011, while the Taliban insurgency grows against Hamid Karzai's government in Afghanistan. In Pakistan, Pervez Musharraf resigns in August and Asif Ali Zardari, widower of the assassinated Benazir Bhutto, becomes president. In November, ten gunmen from the Pakistan-based group Lashkar-e-Taiba attack Mumbai, killing 166 people and straining relations between India, led by Manmohan Singh, and Pakistan. Nepal abolishes its 240-year-old monarchy in May, Bhutan holds its first general election, Iran's President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad faces UN sanctions over its nuclear programme, and on 27 December Israel launches a major offensive against Hamas in Gaza.
regions.north-central-asia: Central Asia's oil and gas states ride high energy prices until the autumn crash: Nursultan Nazarbayev's Kazakhstan, Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow's Turkmenistan, which he has ruled since Saparmurat Niyazov's death in 2006, and Islam Karimov's Uzbekistan. Kurmanbek Bakiyev rules Kyrgyzstan and Emomali Rahmon Tajikistan. In Mongolia, riots break out in July over alleged fraud in parliamentary elections. Siberia's oil and gas fund a resurgent Russia, but the oil price falls by about three-quarters between July and December.
regions.east-asia: China, under President Hu Jintao and Premier Wen Jiabao, has a turbulent year: protests against Chinese rule in Tibet in March are put down, and the Sichuan earthquake in May kills some 69,000 people. But the Beijing Olympic Games in August showcase China's rise, its astronauts make their first spacewalk in September, and as exports slump it announces a 4-trillion-yuan stimulus plan in November. In Taiwan, Ma Ying-jeou is elected president and opens direct flights to the mainland. South Korea's new president, Lee Myung-bak, faces huge protests over US beef imports, North Korea's Kim Jong-il is reported to have suffered a stroke, and Japan, under Emperor Akihito, changes prime minister from Fukuda Yasuo to Aso Taro in September.
regions.southeast-asia: Cyclone Nargis strikes Myanmar's Irrawaddy delta in May, killing at least 138,000 people, while the ruling generals at first restrict foreign aid and push through a new constitution in a referendum. Thailand is in turmoil: anti-government protesters occupy Government House and in late November shut Bangkok's airports, until a court dissolves the ruling party and Abhisit Vejjajiva becomes prime minister in December. Indonesia, led by Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono, sees its former dictator Suharto die in January. Malaysia's ruling coalition loses its two-thirds majority in parliament for the first time since 1969, and Gloria Macapagal Arroyo leads the Philippines.
regions.northern-north-america: Canada's Conservative Prime Minister Stephen Harper formally apologises in June for the residential schools that took Indigenous children from their families, and wins a second minority government in October. As the recession bites, opposition parties plan to bring him down, and in December he has Parliament suspended to avoid a confidence vote. In November, about three-quarters of Greenland's voters approve greater self-government within the Danish realm, to take effect in June 2009.
regions.southern-north-america: The US housing bubble bursts: the investment bank Bear Stearns is rescued in March, the government takes over the mortgage giants Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac in September, Lehman Brothers goes bankrupt on 15 September, and Congress approves a $700 billion bank rescue in October. In November, Democrat Barack Obama defeats John McCain to succeed George W. Bush. Mexico's President Felipe Calderon is waging war on the drug cartels, and more than 5,000 people are murdered in 2008 as violence escalates. Fidel Castro hands Cuba's presidency to his brother Raul in February, and Haiti is shaken by food riots.
regions.northern-south-america: Brazil, under Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, is riding a commodity boom, and huge oil fields have been found deep beneath its seabed. In March, Colombian forces under President Alvaro Uribe kill the FARC commander Raul Reyes in a raid inside Ecuador, and Ecuador and Venezuela move troops to the border; in July, Colombia frees the hostage Ingrid Betancourt and 14 others in a daring rescue. Ecuador's voters approve a new constitution backed by President Rafael Correa, Bolivia's Evo Morales faces violent protests in the eastern departments demanding autonomy, and Hugo Chavez rules Venezuela. In May, South American leaders found the Union of South American Nations (UNASUR).
regions.southern-cone: Argentina's President Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner, in office since December 2007, faces months of farmers' strikes and road blockades after raising export taxes on soybeans in March. In Paraguay, the former bishop Fernando Lugo wins the April election, ending 61 years of rule by the Colorado Party. Michelle Bachelet is Chile's first woman president, and Tabare Vazquez is president of Uruguay.
regions.australasia: Australia's new Labor prime minister, Kevin Rudd, makes a formal national apology on 13 February to the Stolen Generations of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children taken from their families. New Zealand elects John Key's National Party in November, ending Helen Clark's nine years in power. Fiji remains under the military government of Commodore Frank Bainimarama, who seized power in a 2006 coup, and Michael Somare leads Papua New Guinea.

title: Pandemic and War
overview: A new coronavirus, first identified in Wuhan, China, at the end of 2019, spreads around the world in early 2020. The World Health Organization declares COVID-19 a pandemic on 11 March; billions of people live under lockdowns, borders close, and the world economy suffers its worst recession since the Second World War. Vaccines developed at record speed are first given in December 2020. More than 7 million deaths are officially reported, and the WHO estimates that almost 15 million more people than usual died in 2020 and 2021 alone. The years to 2024 bring further shocks. The Taliban retake Afghanistan in 2021. Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 starts the largest war in Europe since 1945 and drives up energy and food prices worldwide. A Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 is followed by a devastating war in Gaza, and in December 2024 Syria's Bashar al-Assad is overthrown. The world's population passes eight billion in November 2022, and India overtakes China as the most populous country in 2023. Artificial-intelligence chatbots such as ChatGPT (2022) spread fast, rivalry between the United States and China sharpens, and 2024 is the warmest year on record.

regions.southern-africa: South Africa, under Cyril Ramaphosa, imposes one of the world's strictest lockdowns, and its scientists detect the Beta variant of the virus in 2020 and help identify Omicron in 2021. In 2024 the ANC loses the parliamentary majority it has held since 1994 and forms a coalition government. In the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, the M23 rebels, which UN experts say are backed by Rwanda, launch a new offensive in 2022, and an Islamist insurgency in northern Mozambique's Cabo Delgado province draws in Rwandan troops in 2021. Samia Suluhu Hassan becomes Tanzania's first woman president after John Magufuli's death in 2021, and Kenya elects William Ruto in 2022.
regions.northern-africa: In November 2020 war breaks out between Ethiopia's government, led by Abiy Ahmed, and the leaders of its Tigray region; by some estimates hundreds of thousands die before a peace deal is signed in Pretoria in November 2022. Sudan's transition after Omar al-Bashir's fall is ended by a coup in 2021, and in April 2023 war erupts between the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces, driving over ten million people from their homes. A wave of military coups sweeps the Sahel, in Mali (2020 and 2021), Guinea (2021), Burkina Faso (twice in 2022) and Niger (2023); the juntas of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger send French troops home and form the Alliance of Sahel States. Abdel Fattah el-Sisi rules Egypt, Tunisia's President Kais Saied suspends parliament in 2021, and in September 2023 an earthquake kills nearly 3,000 people in Morocco and floods devastate Derna in Libya.
regions.europe: Italy is Europe's first coronavirus hotspot, and lockdowns spread across the continent; in July 2020 EU leaders agree a €750 billion recovery fund. Britain leaves the European Union on 31 January 2020. On 24 February 2022 Russia, which annexed Crimea in 2014, launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine; Ukrainian forces under President Volodymyr Zelenskyy drive the invaders back from Kyiv, but fighting grinds on in the east and south, and millions of Ukrainians flee abroad. Finland (2023) and Sweden (2024) join NATO. In Belarus, Alexander Lukashenko crushes mass protests after a disputed 2020 election, and Azerbaijan regains much of Nagorno-Karabakh in a 2020 war and the rest in 2023, when almost all its Armenian population flees. Olaf Scholz succeeds Angela Merkel in Germany in 2021, Emmanuel Macron leads France, Britain has four prime ministers from Boris Johnson to Keir Starmer, and Queen Elizabeth II dies in September 2022.
regions.middle-east-south-asia: India, under Narendra Modi, suffers a devastating wave of the Delta variant in 2021, clashes with Chinese troops in the Galwan valley in 2020, lands a probe near the Moon's south pole in 2023, and in 2024 returns Modi for a third term at the head of a coalition. As US troops withdraw, the Taliban take Kabul on 15 August 2021. Floods put huge areas of Pakistan under water in 2022, economic collapse forces Sri Lanka's president from office the same year, and Bangladesh's Sheikh Hasina resigns and flees in August 2024 after student-led protests. In 2020 the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain establish relations with Israel. On 7 October 2023 a Hamas-led attack kills about 1,200 people in Israel and takes some 250 hostages; Israel's offensive in Gaza kills more than 40,000 Palestinians by late 2024, according to Gaza's health ministry, and fighting spreads to Lebanon and the Red Sea. Mass protests follow the death of Mahsa Amini in Iranian police custody in 2022, an earthquake kills more than 50,000 people in Turkey and Syria in February 2023, and Syria's Bashar al-Assad is overthrown in December 2024.
regions.north-central-asia: In Kyrgyzstan, protests after a disputed election in October 2020 bring Sadyr Japarov to power. In January 2022, deadly unrest in Kazakhstan leads President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev to call in troops from a Russian-led alliance and to remove his predecessor Nursultan Nazarbayev from his remaining post. Turkmenistan's Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow hands the presidency to his son Serdar in 2022, Shavkat Mirziyoyev leads Uzbekistan, and Emomali Rahmon's Tajikistan fights deadly border clashes with Kyrgyzstan in 2021 and 2022. When Russia orders a military call-up in September 2022, hundreds of thousands of Russian men leave the country, many crossing into Kazakhstan.
regions.east-asia: China, under Xi Jinping, seals off Wuhan and then pursues a 'zero-COVID' policy of mass testing and lockdowns until it is abruptly dropped in December 2022, after rare street protests. A national security law imposed on Hong Kong in 2020 ends its protest movement, and Xi begins a third term as Communist Party leader in 2022. Taiwan, led by Tsai Ing-wen and from 2024 by Lai Ching-te, faces large Chinese military exercises. Japan, under Emperor Naruhito, holds the postponed Tokyo Olympics in 2021; Prime Minister Abe Shinzo resigns in 2020 and is assassinated in 2022. North Korea's Kim Jong Un seals his borders and steps up missile tests, and in December 2024 South Korea's President Yoon Suk Yeol briefly declares martial law and is impeached.
regions.southeast-asia: In Myanmar the army seizes power on 1 February 2021 and detains Aung San Suu Kyi; its crackdown on protests turns into a civil war in which armed resistance groups make large gains from late 2023. Ferdinand Marcos Jr., son of the former dictator, is elected president of the Philippines in 2022, succeeding Rodrigo Duterte. Indonesia's Joko Widodo, who begins building a new capital, Nusantara, on Borneo, is followed by Prabowo Subianto, elected in 2024. Thailand sees youth-led protests in 2020, and Anwar Ibrahim becomes Malaysia's prime minister in 2022 after years of political turmoil.
regions.northern-north-america: Canada, under Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, is shaken in 2021 by the discovery of possible unmarked graves at former residential schools for Indigenous children. Truckers protesting vaccine rules blockade Ottawa and border crossings in early 2022, and in 2023 wildfires burn a larger area than in any season on record. Greenland, self-governing within Denmark, draws growing interest as melting Arctic ice opens sea routes and access to minerals, and its 2021 election is fought over a planned rare-earth and uranium mine.
regions.southern-north-america: The United States records more than a million COVID-19 deaths, the most of any country. The murder of George Floyd by a Minneapolis police officer in May 2020 sparks nationwide protests, Joe Biden defeats Donald Trump in November 2020, and Trump's supporters storm the US Capitol on 6 January 2021; in November 2024 Trump is elected again. Mexico elects Claudia Sheinbaum as its first woman president in 2024. Haiti's President Jovenel Moise is assassinated in 2021, and armed gangs take over much of Port-au-Prince, while El Salvador's Nayib Bukele jails tens of thousands in a sweeping crackdown on gangs from 2022.
regions.northern-south-america: Brazil, under Jair Bolsonaro, records some 700,000 COVID-19 deaths, and Peru reports the world's highest death rate. Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva returns as Brazil's president in January 2023, a week before Bolsonaro's supporters storm government buildings in Brasilia. Peru's President Pedro Castillo is removed and arrested in December 2022 after trying to dissolve Congress. Nearly eight million Venezuelans have left their country, and Nicolas Maduro claims victory in a disputed July 2024 election. Colombia elects its first left-wing president, Gustavo Petro, in 2022, Ecuador's President Daniel Noboa declares war on drug gangs in January 2024, and an oil boom makes Guyana one of the world's fastest-growing economies.
regions.southern-cone: Argentina, battered by the pandemic and by inflation approaching 200 percent a year, elects the libertarian outsider Javier Milei, who takes office in December 2023 promising to slash the state; Argentina also wins the 2022 football World Cup. In Chile, Gabriel Boric is elected president in 2021 after mass protests, but voters reject two proposed new constitutions, in 2022 and 2023. Paraguay elects Santiago Pena in 2023, Uruguay elects Yamandu Orsi in November 2024, and in 2024 the worst floods in its history devastate Brazil's southern state of Rio Grande do Sul.
regions.australasia: Australia and New Zealand close their borders and keep COVID-19 deaths low through 2020 and 2021. New Zealand's Jacinda Ardern wins a landslide in 2020 and steps down in 2023, and Christopher Luxon becomes prime minister later that year. Under the AUKUS pact (2021), Australia is to gain nuclear-powered submarines with American and British help; Anthony Albanese becomes prime minister in 2022, and Australians reject an Indigenous Voice to Parliament in a 2023 referendum. The Hunga Tonga undersea volcano erupts with enormous force in January 2022, and deadly unrest breaks out in New Caledonia in 2024 over voting rules.
